The Sticker on the Wrong Parcel

贴错包裹的标签 · 644 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A commercial carrier brought fifteen parcels by rail to a warehouse beside the station. One shipment contained electrical equipment for a school, including a laptop charger. A second held food bought in bulk by a grocer. When the school clerk opened her package, she found a frozen ham. The dealer insisted his laptop had left the warehouse that morning. He reported a possible theft and offered a copy of the invoice as proof. Noor, who ran the storage room, asked for the transport receipt before anyone tried to blame a driver.

2The receipt gave a single destination for the equipment. A freight scanner showed that it had reached the station. The scan was reliable. It could not compute the actual weight or show what a carton contained. Noor found two stickers on the food box. One bore a low postage charge and a different carrier's name. The other carried authorization for a school delivery. A detailed log said that a worker in uniform had applied both before his shift ended. Noor telephoned him.

3A scratch on a reusable bin reminded the worker what he had done. He had moved a damaged sticker without opening the carton. A backpack and a briefcase were on the same rack. A member of staff leaving on an excursion had put a beverage there. The carrier had a separate restriction on sending liquor and cigarettes. Sorting personal and commercial goods together made those rules harder to enforce. One mixed bench offered convenience at the expense of a reliable record.

4Noor compared the quantity and weight. The ham was nearly five kilos. The laptop weighed less than half that, including protective wrapping. The school invoice gave pounds and ounces, while the grocer's receipt used kilograms. After conversion, the difference was convincing. Noor asked the grocer's personnel to verify which carton had reached cold storage. He found a dry package beside an empty bin. It was apparently meant for a scale, so nobody had opened it.

5The grocer returned at sunset. Under the outer wrapping was a second sticker bearing the same invoice number as the school's. The laptop lay inside. The grocer's account was truthful. Nobody stole the laptop. Noor still had to notify the school and trace the food. The ham had spent hours outside its cold store. She set it aside for disposal and arranged a refund, keeping the two claims separate.

6The depot also revised its claim procedure. A stolen item had to be identified by a serial number and the original receipt. A leaking parcel needed a separate form. An employee could not simply dump it with the other waste. The manager tested both routes with an ordinary carton and a small cash deposit. One person could furnish evidence of a shipment without being asked to prove who had meant to steal it. The new form closed that loophole.

7The carrier proposed a scanner upgrade. Noor asked it to standardize the label and simplify the transaction first. The worker would check weight, destination, and contents before he moved a sticker. The scan was the cornerstone of the tracking system, but a label could be copied. A second worker would examine a valuable parcel and confirm timely delivery. The new procedure did not let anyone reset a record without an explanation. It reduced reliance on memory without slowing every parcel.

8A week later the school collected the equipment. Noor showed the clerk the weight on the bottom and a copy of the import form. The transportation company used the same rule for items it would export. One sticker could not be the sole record of a delivery. A responsible worker would look for the invoice before offering to haul a valuable box. Noor moved the backpack shelf by the door. The next worker could see which items were meant for storage and which were waiting for shipment.

贴错包裹的标签

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1商业承运商用铁路把十五个包裹送到车站旁的仓库。一批是给学校的电器，里面有笔记本电脑的充电器。另一批是杂货商批量购进的食品。校方职员打开箱子，却找到一块冻火腿。经销商坚称笔记本上午就出库了，怀疑有人偷窃，还拿出发票复印件作证。管库房的努尔先要看运输收据，免得大家急着怪司机。

2收据只写了一个设备目的地。货运扫描显示箱子已到车站。扫描本身可信，却量不出实际重量，也看不见箱里的东西。努尔发现食品箱上有两张贴纸，一张是较低的邮费和另一家承运商的名称，另一张授权送学校。详细日志记着，一位穿制服的工人在下班前贴过两张。努尔给他打了电话。

3一只周转箱的刮痕让工人想起，他把破损的贴纸移走时没打开箱子。同一架上有背包和公文包，一名要外出的职员还把饮料放在那里。承运商另有限制寄送烈酒和香烟的规定。个人物品和商业货物混在一起，规则也难执行。混用一张分拣台虽方便，记录却不容易可靠。

4努尔对了件数和重量。火腿近五公斤，笔记本连防护包装都不到一半。学校发票用磅和盎司，杂货商用千克。换成同一单位后，差距很清楚。努尔请杂货店人员核对哪箱进了冷藏库。他在空箱旁找到一份干的包裹，看着像要送来装秤的，所以没人打开。

5日落时，杂货商回来了。外包装下有第二张贴纸，发票号和学校的一样，电脑就在里面。杂货商没说假话，也没人偷电脑。努尔还得通知学校，追查食品去了哪里。火腿已经离开冷库几个小时，她先单独放好等处理，再安排退款，两项索赔分开办。

6货站也改了索赔流程。报失的物品要用序列号和原始收据确认。渗漏的包裹得另填表，工作人员不能随便倒进垃圾里。主管拿普通纸箱和一小笔押金试了两条流程。人们可以提供运输证据，不必先证明谁打算偷东西。新表堵上了这个漏洞。

7承运商提议升级扫描仪，努尔请他们先统一标签、简化交接。移动贴纸前，工人得对重量、目的地和内容。扫描是跟踪的基础，但贴纸本来就能复制。贵重件再请第二人查看，确认按时送达。新流程还要求重设记录必须说明原因。这样能减少靠记忆做事，也不会拖慢每一个包裹。

8一周后，学校收到了设备。努尔给职员看箱底的重量和进口表的副本。运输公司对出口货也用同一规则。一张贴纸承担不了整次交付的记录。负责的工人答应搬贵重箱前，会先看发票。努尔把放背包的架子搬到门边。下一个工人一看就知道，哪些东西是暂存的，哪些正在等发货。
